facts.fact_text: In April 2003 a group of farmers held a demonstration in front of the Seimas (the Lithuanian Parliament) building.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the situation in the agricultural sector with regard to a fall in wholesale prices for various agricultural products.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the lack of subsidies for producing agricultural products.
The farmers demonstrating in April 2003 demanded that the State take action regarding the situation in the agricultural sector.
The demonstrations started on 19 May 2003.
The farmers gathered in the designated areas on 19 May 2003.
On 21 May 2003 the farmers blocked and continued to demonstrate on the roads next to Dirvupiai village, on the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
On 21 May 2003 the farmers blocked and continued to demonstrate at the sixty-third kilometre of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.
On 21 May 2003 the farmers blocked and continued to demonstrate at the ninety-fourth kilometre of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway.
Pre-trial investigations against the applicants and a number of other persons were started on suspicion of having caused a riot.
In July 2003 Mr Bronius Markauskas, Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Artūras Pilota and Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas were ordered not to leave their place of residence.
The applicants submitted that on 1 October 2003 the police had imposed a fine of 40 Lithuanian litai (approximately 12 euros) on farmer A.D.

According to the applicants, the police record relating to the fine on farmer A.D. established that on 21 May 2003 A.D. had taken the farmers to block the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway in Kalvarija municipality.
Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius were accused of incitement to riot under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor noted that Mr Bronius Markauskas had taken part in the farmers' meeting of 16 May 2003, at which the farmers had decided to hold demonstrations near major highways on 19 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that at the 16 May 2003 meeting, the farmers had decided that should the Government not grant their requirements by 11 a.m. on 21 May 2003, they would blockade those highways.
The prosecutor noted that on 19 May 2003 Mr Bronius Markauskas had told the farmers to blockade the roads on 21 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that as a result of Mr Bronius Markauskas's incitement, at 12.09 p.m. on 21 May 2003 around 500 farmers had gone on to the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
The prosecutor noted that the farmers had refused to obey police requests not to stand on the Vilnius-Klaipėda road.
The prosecutor noted that as a consequence of the blockade of the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway, traffic had been blocked until 1 p.m. on 23 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that traffic jams had occurred on neighbouring roads and road transport in the region had become impossible as a result of the blockade of the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
The prosecutor claimed that Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had incited the farmers to blockade the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.

The prosecutor claimed that as a result of Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius's incitement, at midday on 21 May 2003 around 250 people had gone on to the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway, refusing police orders not to block the highway.
The prosecutor claimed that the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga road had remained blocked until 10.58 a.m. on 23 May 2003.
The prosecutor claimed that the roads in the vicinity of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway had become clogged as a result of the blockade.
The prosecutor claimed that the normal functioning of the Saločiai-Grenctale border control post had been interrupted as a result of the blockade of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.
Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota were accused of a serious breach of public order during the riot, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor established that on 21 May 2003, at around 11.50 a.m., around 1,500 people had gone on to the ninety-fourth kilometre of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway.

The prosecutor established that at about 3-4 p.m. on 21 May 2003, Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had driven on to the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway with three tractors and had left the tractors on the asphalt carriageway.

The prosecutor established that Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had refused to obey police instructions not to breach public order and not to leave the tractors on the road.
The prosecutor established that the tractors had remained on the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai road until 4.15 p.m. on 23 May 2003.
The prosecutor established that as a result of the blockade, the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway had been blocked from the eighty-fourth to the ninety-fourth kilometre.
The prosecutor established that due to the resulting increase of traffic on neighbouring roads, congestion had built up and car transport in the region had come to a halt.

The prosecutor established that the normal functioning of the Kalvarija and Marijampolė State border control posts had been disrupted as a result of the blockade of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway.

Within the criminal proceedings, a logistics company brought a civil claim against Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius, as the person who had incited the farmers to block the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga road, seeking damages of 1,100 Lithuanian litai (approximately 290 euros) for the loss allegedly incurred due to the blockade of that road.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
In convicting Mr Bronius Markauskas, the Kaunas City District Court relied on video recordings of the events, documentary evidence and the testimony of one witness.
The Kaunas City District Court concluded that Mr Bronius Markauskas had organised a gathering with the aim of seriously violating public order, that is to say a riot.

The Kaunas City District Court found that Mr Bronius Markauskas had been one of the leaders of the farmers' meeting on 16 May 2003, at which the farmers had decided to attempt to achieve their goals by organising protests next to trunk roads.

The Kaunas City District Court found that Mr Bronius Markauskas had coordinated the actions of the farmers and as a consequence on 21 May 2003 around 500 people had gone to the Vilnius-Klaipėda road and had blocked it.
The Kaunas City District Court found that as a result of Mr Bronius Markauskas's actions, car traffic on the Vilnius-Klaipėda road had been blocked until 23 May 2003.

The Kaunas City District Court established, mainly on the basis of video recordings and documentary evidence, that Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had organised a gathering with the aim of seriously breaching public order.
The Kaunas City District Court established that Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had taken part in the farmers' meeting of 16 May 2003 and had known about the decision to hold protests next to the roads.

The Kaunas City District Court established that when a crowd of farmers had blocked the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga road on 21 May 2003, public order had been seriously breached, car traffic had stopped at that part of the road, causing inconvenience to drivers and goods carriers.

The Kaunas City District Court established that during the blockade of 21 and 22 May 2003, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius coordinated the actions of the crowd by giving orders that some of the vehicles should be let through.
The Kaunas City District Court established that during the blockade of 21 and 22 May 2003, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius incited the farmers to hold on and not to move away from the highway.

The Kaunas City District Court established that during the blockade of 21 and 22 May 2003, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius was in contact with the participants in the protests in Kalvarija municipality and Klaipėda region.
The Kaunas City District Court established that during the blockade of 21 and 22 May 2003, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius was negotiating with the authorities by mobile phone in the name of the farmers.
The Kaunas City District Court emphasised that the farmers who had gathered obeyed the actions of Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius and followed his orders.
The Kaunas City District Court qualified the actions of Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius as organising riots under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.

On the basis of written evidence submitted by Linava (the Lithuanian National Road Carriers' Association), the Kaunas City District Court found that by having organised the blockade of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga road, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had seriously breached public order and had caused pecuniary damage to three carrier companies.
As one of the carriers had submitted a civil claim in the sum of 1,100 Lithuanian litai, the Kaunas City District Court deemed it proper to grant it.

In finding Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota guilty of rioting, the Kaunas City District Court relied on documentary evidence, audiovisual materials and two witnesses' testimony.

The Kaunas City District Court established that on 21 May 2003 between 11.50 a.m. and 4.15 p.m., Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had driven tractors on to the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway at its ninety-fourth kilometre.

The Kaunas City District Court established that Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had refused to obey lawful requirements by the police not to breach public order and not to park the tractors on the road.

The Kaunas City District Court established that Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had kept the tractors on the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway until 4.15 p.m. on 22 May 2003.

The Kaunas City District Court established that because about 1,500 people had gathered on the road, the traffic had been blocked between the eighty-fourth and ninety-fourth kilometres of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai road.

The Kaunas City District Court established that traffic jams had occurred and the normal functioning of the Kalvarija and Lazdijai border control offices had been disrupted as a result of the blockade of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway.
The five applicants were each given a sixty-day custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) by the Kaunas City District Court.

The applicants were ordered not to leave their places of residence for more than seven days without the authorities' prior agreement, for a period of one year whilst execution of the sentence was suspended.
Pre-trial investigations against the applicants and a number of other persons were started on suspicion of having caused a riot.
The applicants submitted that on 1 October 2003 the police had imposed a fine of 40 Lithuanian litai (approximately 12 euros) on farmer A.D.

According to the applicants, by his actions A.D. had breached paragraph 81 of the Road Traffic Rules and thus committed an administrative law violation as provided for in Article 131 of the Code of Administrative Law Offences.
On 4 December 2003 an indictment was brought before the courts.
Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius were accused of incitement to riot under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor claimed that Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had incited the farmers to blockade the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.
Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota were accused of a serious breach of public order during the riot, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code establishes criminal liability for rioting, which is categorised as a public order offence.

Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code provides that a person who has organised or provoked a gathering of persons to commit public acts of violence, damage property or seriously breach public order in other ways, or a person who, during a riot, has committed acts of violence, damaged property or seriously breached public order in other ways, may be sentenced to a custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) or imprisonment for up to five years.

Article 75 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code stipulates that if a person is sentenced to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years for the commission of one or several minor or less serious premeditated crimes, a court may suspend the sentence imposed for a period ranging from one to three years.

Article 75 § 2 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code stipulates that the sentence may be suspended when the court rules that there is a sufficient basis for believing that the purpose of the penalty will be achieved without the sentence actually being served.

Article 75 § 2 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code provides that when suspending execution of the sentence, the court may order the convicted person not to leave his place of residence for a period of longer than seven days, without prior agreement of the authority which supervises execution of the judgment.
Pursuant to Article 97 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code, individuals convicted of a crime and whose conviction has become effective are considered as people with a previous conviction.
Pursuant to Article 97 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code, any person given a suspended sentence is considered as having a previous conviction during the period of suspension of the sentence.

Article 31 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code defines the concept of necessity (būtinasis reikalingumas), stating that a person shall not be held liable under the criminal law for an act committed in an attempt to avert an immediate danger which threatens him, other persons or their rights, or public or State interests, where this danger could not have been averted by other means and where the damage caused is less than the damage which it is intended to avert.

Article 31 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code provides that a person who creates a dangerous situation by his actions may only rely upon the defence of necessity when the dangerous situation arose through negligence (dėl neatsargumo).

Article 1241 of the Lithuanian Code of Administrative Law Offences at the relevant time provided for administrative liability for a breach of traffic rules by drivers, stipulating that a breach of the rules on how and when a driver could stop and park on highways carried a fine from 100 to 150 Lithuanian litai (approximately 30-45 euros).

Article 131 of the Lithuanian Code of Administrative Law Offences provided for administrative liability for non-observance by pedestrians of traffic signals, crossing of a carriageway or walking on it, punishable by a fine of 30-50 Lithuanian litai (approximately 8-15 euros).
Point 81 of the Lithuanian Road Traffic Rules provided that pedestrians must walk on the sidewalk and, if there is none, on the right side of the road in a single line.
Article 62 (2) of the Constitution of the Republic of Lithuania states that a member of the Parliament may not be held criminally liable without the consent of the Parliament.

Article 49 (1) of the Lithuanian Law on Parliamentary Elections provides that without the consent of the Central Electoral Commission, during an election campaign as well as until the first meeting of a newly-elected Parliament, a parliamentary candidate may not be charged with a crime or arrested and his or her freedom may not be restricted in any other way.

Later in May 2003, four companies that transport goods informed the police and Linava, the Lithuanian National Road Carriers' Association, that they had sustained pecuniary damage in the sum of 25,235 Lithuanian litai (approximately 7,300 euros) due to the blockade of the roads during the farmers' demonstrations.
The four transport companies stated that they would institute civil proceedings in respect of their claims for pecuniary damage caused by the blockade of the roads during the farmers' demonstrations.
The prosecutor noted that traffic jams had occurred on neighbouring roads and road transport in the region had become impossible as a result of the blockade of the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
The prosecutor claimed that the roads in the vicinity of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway had become clogged as a result of the blockade.
The prosecutor claimed that the normal functioning of the Saločiai-Grenctale border control post had been interrupted as a result of the blockade of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.
The prosecutor established that due to the resulting increase of traffic on neighbouring roads, congestion had built up and car transport in the region had come to a halt.

The prosecutor established that the normal functioning of the Kalvarija and Marijampolė State border control posts had been disrupted as a result of the blockade of the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway.

On the basis of written evidence submitted by Linava (the Lithuanian National Road Carriers' Association), the Kaunas City District Court found that by having organised the blockade of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga road, Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had seriously breached public order and had caused pecuniary damage to three carrier companies.
The Kaunas Regional Court found that the actions of Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had caused damage to goods carriers and had thus seriously breached public order.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that by driving tractors on to the road, causing traffic congestion and disturbing the work of the State border control service, and by refusing to obey lawful requests by the police not to park their tractors on the road, Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had seriously breached public order.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that the fact that after the roads had been blocked the police and the drivers had negotiated with the farmers with the result that some of the drivers had been let through did not diminish the danger of the offence and its unlawfulness.

The Kaunas Regional Court emphasised that the blockade of a major highway (magistralinis kelias) had had dangerous consequences and could not be considered to have been a mere administrative law offence such as a traffic violation.

In providing an explanation of the substance of the crime of rioting under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code, the Supreme Court referred to the classification of the offence as an offence against public order.

The Supreme Court established that Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code stipulated the following features of the crime of rioting: the organisation of a gathering with the aim of causing public violence, damaging property or breaching public order in other ways, or the commission of those actions during a gathering.
The Supreme Court found that a riot was to be characterised as a situation when a gathering of people deliberately seriously breached public order, caused public violence, or damaged property.

The Supreme Court stated that the applicants had not been sentenced for expressing their opinion or imparting ideas, actions protected by Article 10 § 1 of the Convention, but for actions by which they had seriously breached public order.
The Supreme Court held that the applicants' dissatisfaction with the Government's agricultural policy had not justified the acts for which the five applicants had been convicted.

At the 16 May 2003 meeting of the Chamber of Agriculture, one of the measures foreseen if no positive changes in legal regulation were forthcoming was addressing complaints to the administrative courts.

The Kaunas City District Court dismissed Mr Bronius Markauskas's claim that he and other farmers had acted out of necessity because the roadblock had been their last opportunity to draw the Government's attention to their problems.

The Kaunas City District Court found that the farmers had had another alternative, namely bringing complaints before the administrative courts, which the farmers had themselves mentioned during the meeting of 16 May 2003.

The Kaunas City District Court noted that under Article 31 § 2 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code, a person who created a dangerous situation by his or her actions could only rely on the defence of necessity when a dangerous situation arose through negligence.

The Kaunas Regional Court established that Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had understood that the roadblocks would be illegal and that they had been warned about their liability as organisers.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that despite being warned, Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had kept coordinating the farmers' actions and had insisted that farmers would maintain the roadblocks.

The Kaunas Regional Court emphasised that the behaviour of Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius, in guiding the actions of the other individuals involved in the protest, could not be regarded as a non-punishable expression of their opinion, because they had breached public order by their actions, for which criminal liability was foreseen.

The Kaunas Regional Court stated that the criminal offence had not lost its element of public danger merely because the Government had refused to raise wholesale prices or because the Government had allegedly failed to take necessary action.

The Kaunas Regional Court noted that the crime at issue had been committed in May 2003, whilst the Central Electoral Commission had registered Mr Bronius Markauskas as a candidate in the Parliamentary elections only in September 2004.
The Supreme Court shared the appellate court's view that the applicants could not be considered as having acted out of necessity.

The Supreme Court held that the fall in milk purchase prices and other problems with subsidies for agriculture had not constituted a clear or present danger to someone's property, because the property in question had not yet materialised.
The Supreme Court held that the law protects existing property and that the State had not deprived the applicants of their property.
The Supreme Court held that the applicants' dissatisfaction with the Government's agricultural policy had not justified the acts for which the five applicants had been convicted.
